title: Junta restriction failure and empirical error
statement: Let $n,k,M\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix a sign assignment $z$ on $P$. Suppose $|P|\le k$, and let $\delta$ satisfy $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$. For every sequence of $2^{k+1}M$ plus the Fourier estimator sample count at accuracy $2^{-(k+1)}$ and failure parameter $\delta$ cube inputs, if fewer than $M$ inputs agree with $z$ on all coordinates in $P$, then the absolute difference between the empirical fraction agreeing with $z$ and its uniform-cube probability is at least $2^{-(k+1)}$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function on the n-dimensional sign cube
Sample sequence has the defined junta restriction sample count
